sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: dergfhlaith is an Irish ritual drink. The name means 'the dark-red ale of sovereignty.' Derg means dark red. Flaith means sovereignty. Laith means ale. MacKillop gives the sense as red sovereignty and reads the word as a pun on flaith and laith. The drink sealed the union of the king and the earth goddess. The earth goddess offered it to the king at his inauguration. The custom had Continental Celtic antecedents. Scholars disagreed about its origin. It may have evolved when Celtic invaders met an older goddess-centered culture. The red ale bound the king to the land. It placed sacred vows and responsibilities on him. These were the geis and buada specific to his region. They also demanded the generosity and nobility required of all Irish kings. Some myths connect the ale to Medb. Medb was the goddess of sovereignty humanized into the great queen of Connacht. The ale is also associated with the land goddesses Ériu and Flaith. The story of Conn Cétchathach pictures the drink directly. Conn dreamed that Sovereignty handed him the red ale instead of taking him to her bed. He and his descendants kept drinking of it after that gift.

okr.objective: Describe the Irish inaugural drink dergfhlaith, its name, and its role in binding king and land.
key_results: Explain the roots derg, flaith, and laith, and the pun that MacKillop records.
Describe the inauguration offering by the earth goddess and its Continental Celtic antecedents.

Tell the dream of Conn Cétchathach, in which Sovereignty gave him the red ale instead of her bed.
